classification.difficultyReason: Extract the right-triangle cross-section from the tent illustration, treating the middle height as opposite and the sloping side as hypotenuse, then apply inverse sine.

content.prompt: A tent with a simple A-frame design is set up as a shelter. Each sloping side of its triangular cross-section is 2.9 metres long, as shown. Find the angle to the ground that the sides of the tent make if the height at the middle of the shelter is 1.5 metres. Round your answer to the nearest 0.1 of a degree.

spec.description: Perspective A-frame tent with an open front triangular cross-section, highlighted dashed baseline and altitude, and 2.9 m beside the rear sloping roof edge. The source does not print the height on the diagram.
spec.mathematics: The height is 1.5 m in the stem. The diagram positions 2.9 m as a sloping side, while the stem describes a horizontal half-breadth; these interpretations produce different angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated angle is supplied.

answer.worked:
In half of the triangular cross-section, opposite $=1.5$ m and hypotenuse $=2.9$ m. Use sine.
$$\begin{align*}\sin\theta&=\frac{O}{H}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{1.5}{2.9}\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1.5}{2.9}\right)\\\theta&\approx31.1^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
